Just 33% of respondents in the four-day survey said they approved of Trump's performance in the White House, while 64% disapproved. Trump's approval rating, down from 35% in a poll that closed earlier this month and ​lower than at any point in his current term, has now tied the lowest level of his prior term reached in December 2017.

results.content: Donald Trump’s net approval rating remains in the dumps at -26, according to The Economist’s tracker of YouGov polling. On September 9th the president will begin a two-day rally in Dallas, Texas—an oddity outside a presidential-election year. The jamboree is intended to gin up Republican support ahead of the midterms. Perhaps the organisers have been watching Mr Trump’s poll numbers. Seemingly worried about low-attendance, the party has been offering free tickets. [...] Using YouGov’s data, The Economist has projected Mr Trump’s approval rating state by state. results.content: The drop in approval rating is in part driven by growing dissatisfaction even among Republicans. Between July and August, Trump’s approval rating with Republican voters fell from 82% to 77%, according to polls. It’s the only group for which Trump’s approval rating is above 50%, as he is underwater with voters of every race, gender and age group. [...] It’s the lowest approval rating recorded by the Elon poll since Trump took office in January 2025, and data suggests it may be among the lowest approval ratings in recent history for a president in North Carolina.
